answer: A Registered domain bound by DNS record proof with annual re-verification turns a private channel into public evidence: the registered domain answers a fresh challenge, the DNS record proof is recorded, and annual re-verification keeps one channel from spawning many identities, so anyone can check that the identity is backed by a real, reachable channel. A jetty out of place triggers the check: the claim is frozen until its channel clears. Between a prism and a plume lies the whole point: Sybils are cheap to make but expensive to bind.
